result:
Solution 2's answer of 171 is correct. I checked the reduction and the lower bound myself. I did not verify the construction at n = 171 in detail, so that step rests on the solution's argument and on my recollection that 171 is the known answer.

**Reduction.** Take two distinct primes p and q below 100. Banana's response is a function r on the queried points. It is consistent with period p exactly when r is constant on each residue class mod p. It is consistent with both periods exactly when r is constant on each component of the graph whose edges join points that are congruent mod p or mod q.

- If that graph has at least two components, a nonconstant r is consistent with both periods, so Ana cannot tell p from q.
- If the graph is connected, r must be constant. A constant r can come from a nonconstant p-periodic f only if some residue mod p is unqueried. So Ana distinguishes p from q exactly when the graph is connected and at least one of the two primes has all its residues queried.

**Conditions on the query set.** At most one prime below 100 can have an unqueried residue. Also, for every pair of primes, the bipartite graph between the queried residues mod p and mod q must be connected.

**Lower bound.** Each query point gives one edge in that bipartite graph, so a connected graph needs at least (residues mod p queried) + (residues mod q queried) − 1 edges. Consider which prime is allowed to be non-full.

- If the non-full prime is 97, the pair (83, 89) has both primes full. It needs 83 + 89 − 1 = 171 edges.
- If it is 89, the pair (83, 97) needs 83 + 97 − 1 = 179 edges.
- If it is 83 or if every prime is full, the pair (89, 97) needs 89 + 97 − 1 = 185 edges.
- If it is any other prime, the pair (89, 97) is full and again needs 185 edges.

So at least 171 queries are necessary. Solution 3's 185 and Solution 1's 186 come from forcing every prime to be full, which is not required.

**Sufficiency.** Solution 2 constructs a 171-point set. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem the residues mod different primes can be chosen independently, so all pairs can be made connected at once, with 97 left non-full.

Solution 1 and Solution 3 do not match this value, so only Solution 2 is correct.

CHOICE: 2
